*J U D G M E N T*

This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioner, U/S 166 of M.V. Act, claiming compensation of Rs.1,50,000/, on account of damage to the vehicle bearing registration No.KA57F1835, in a road traffic accident.

*FACTS OF THE CASE IN NUTSHELL*
2. Facts leading to the case of the petitioner forthcoming in the petition that, on 8.5.2018, at about 7.40 a.m., the driver of petitioner corporation was driving the BMTC Volvo Bus bearing registration Bangalore Metropolitan vs ) Shri Pradeep.V on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61948013/
1 No.KA57F1835 on his schedule trip of The day from Oreka company to Kempegowda bus stop,
slowly and cautiously by following all traffic rules and regulations.

entities.text: BMTC Volvo Bus bearing registration Bangalore Metropolitan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
When the said bus reached at Intel company gate, and was in process of taking left turn towards main road, at that point of time,
the driver of Tata ACE goods bearing registration No.KA04AA4212, came from wrong side in a rash and negligent manner, and dashed to the left side portion of the petitioner's vehicle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner's vehicle front windshield glass was completely broken.
And left side bumper and body shape of the said Volvo bus were damaged.
3. It is alleged in the petition that, after the incident, bus was sent to depot for necessary repairs and replacement of damages.

The petitioner had spent Rs.11,576/ towards repair of the vehicle,
cancellation of trip on 8.5.2018 total loss is a sum of Rs.9,512/ and the said bus was unable to give service to the public for six days due to the alleged accident, said bus incurred huge loss of a sum of Rs.14,000/ per day.
For six days, it works out to Rs.84,000/ and a sum of Rs.45,000/ towards damages and other expenses incurred by the corporation in the process of accident.

4. Further stated that, the Airport traffic police have registered the criminal case, in connection with the accident in question, in Cr.No.35/2018, against the driver of the offending vehicle, for the offences punishable under section 279 of I.P.C and u/s.115, 177, 3(1), 181, 5, 180, 56, 192 of IMV Act.

As such, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2, being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner, towards the damages caused to the vehicle in question, belonged to the petitioner.
5. After registration of the case, as usual notices were issued to the respondents.
In response to the notices, the respondent No.1 remained absence and placed exparte.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 made its appearance through counsel and filed the written statement, in answer to the case of the petitioner.
6. In the written statement of the respondent No.2, has denied the accident and the involvement of the Container Lorry in the accident.
Further admitted about the insurance, subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Further contended that, neither owner of the offending vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of Section 134(2) and Section 158(6)
of Motor Vehicles Act in furnishing better particulars.
And contended that the accident took place in n the year 2018 and the petition was filed in the year 2021.

It is the main contention of the respondent No.2 that, the jurisdictional police after thorough investigation have filed charge sheet under Sec.3(1) R/w 181 and Sec.4 R/w 180 of M.V.Act, stating that, the driver of offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective DL as on the date of accident and thereby owner of the vehicle committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
And also the offending vehicle was not having valid FC and RC to ply in the place of accident.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against their company.

7. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, for final determination of this case,
following issues were framed:
*ISSUES*
Bangalore Metropolitan vs ) Shri Pradeep.V on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61948013/
2 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, its BMTC Volvo Bus bearing registration No.KA57F1835 has damaged in an accident that occurred on 08.05.2018 at about 7.40 a.m., near Orreca Company Gate i.e. Service Road, Devarabisanahalli,
Bengaluru due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tata ACE Goods Vehicle bearing Regn. No.KA04AA4212 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3. What order or award?
8.

In order to substantiate its case, the petitioner corporation the driver of Bus by name Srinivasa.T.N, during the course of evidence, placed his affidavit evidence in lieu of examination inchief, who examined as PW1.
At the time of his evidence, placed his affidavit evidence and 12 documentary evidence got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P12.
In addition to this, placed the evidence of PW2 Wilson Lobo.
At the time of his evidence, documents got marked as Ex.P.13 to Ex.P.21.
On the other hand, to prove the defenses of the respondent No.2, placed the evidence of the Legal Manager by name Sandeep.S.K. as RW1.
At the time of his evidence, one document got marked as Ex.R1.
Hence, the matter was set down for arguments.
9. Heard the arguments of both the counsel.
And perused the materials available on record.
At the time of argument, learned counsel for the petitioner placed written argument for consideration.

10. Consequently, on appreciation of the evidence available on record, my findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order
for the following:

R E A S O N S ISSUE NO.1:
11.

It is my humble opinion that, since the facts of the case has been narrated in detail above, once again, narration of the assertion of the petitioner and the defenses' of the respondent No.2 forthcoming in the written statement is not required herein.

12. Firstly, in connection with ownership of the vehicle bearing registration No.KA57F1835 is concerned, in the evidence of PW1 Srinivasa T.N. stated that, the petitioner BMTC is the owner of the vehicle in question.
He is working as driver cum conductor of the said vehicle.

On 8.5.2018 at about 7.40 a.m., when he was on duty of the BMTC Volvo bus bearing registration No.KA57F 1835, met with an accident, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Tata ACE goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA04AA 4212.
Consequently, bus was damaged.

In support of the said Bangalore Metropolitan vs ) Shri Pradeep.V on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61948013/
3 affidavit evidence, the PW1 on behalf of the petitioner placed, Ex.P.4 to Ex.P.7 for consideration.
The said documents are police documents.

On going through the said documents, it reflect that, on the basis of first information given by PW1, on the same date of the accident criminal law set in motion against the driver of Tata ACE bearing registration No.KA04 AA4212 alleging that, he had committed the offence punishable under Sec.279 of IPC.

After due investigation process, final report has been submitted against the driver of the said vehicle by name Rakshith Gowda and also against the owner of said vehicle on the allegation that, they have committed the offences punishable under Sec. 279 of IPC and under Sec. 115, 117, 3(1), 181, 5, 180, 56 and 192 of Motor Vehicles Act.
13. On the other hand, the recitals of spot mahazar, spot sketch and complaint marked at Ex.P.6 and Ex.P.7, supports the final report submitted by the investigation officer.
On perusal of all these documents, it is crystal clear that, in the accident in question, vehicle belonged to the petitioner was damaged.
The said vehicle was defending vehicle in the said accident.

14. Secondly, it is the assertion of the petitioner through the evidence of PW1 that, due to the accident, left side portion of the bus was damaged, front wind shield glass was completely broken,
left side bumper and body shape damaged.

Due to the said damages, bus in question was unable to complete the schedule trip on the said day and the corporation was suffered loss in toto of Rs.1,50,000/.
15.

in support of the said stand of the PW1 placed his authorization letter, trip sheet, conductor trip sheet, job card, IMV report, income and expenditure document, free licence and driving licence marked as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.3.
Ex. P.8
to Ex.P.12
for consideration.
In the recitals of the Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.3, there is a clear narration about the vehicle number and name of the driver deputed as on the date of the accident.
And route also been noted in the said documents.
As per the Ex.P.9, towards front side wind screen glass, front left side shape of the bus was damaged.
Ex . P.10
discloses about the loss.
But in support of the said document, to show the actual loss, no other supportive documentary evidence is available on record.

16. Over all appreciation of the evidence of the PW1 along with the documentary evidence, there is no dispute that, due to the accident, vehicle of the petitioner corporation was damaged and also there is no dispute with respect to the ownership of the vehicle in question.
Further, on going through the Ex.P.11 and Ex.P.12, it is evident that, at the time of accident, the driver of the vehicle belong to the petitioner had valid and effective driving license.

At the time of crossexamination of PW1, he stated that, he being the driver of the bus belong to the petitioner, as on the date of accident, was proceeding along with workers of the company, at that time offending vehicle came and caused the accident and he gave complaint to the police.
In this regard, both the vehicles were seized and the vehicle pertaining to the petitioner was taken to the interim custody, after two days of the accident.
And denied the suggestion of other side that, due to his sole negligence, accident in question had taken place and false complaint has been given against the driver of the offending vehicle.
But, no important points culled out from the mouth of this witness to show that, the vehicle of the petitioner was not damaged in the accident.
Bangalore Metropolitan vs ) Shri Pradeep.

V on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61948013/
4 17.
In support of the defences forthcoming in the written statement of the respondent No.1, its legal manager, Sandeep.S.K. was examined as RW1.
No whisper in his evidence by denying the damages caused to the vehicle of the petitioner.
At the time of crossexamination of this witness, nothing is forthcoming to say that, the vehicle belonged to the petitioner was not damaged in the accident.
Hence, I am of the view that, in support of the above issue, the petitioner corporation has placed satisfactory evidence for consideration.

18. It is relevant to note that, for compensation filed U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident, only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required, as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in, 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others).
"

entities.text: 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, It was observed that, "When the accident, from the driver of the offending vehicle is proved, clearly indicates that, due to the said mistake on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, the defending vehicle was damaged."
19. In the light of my due discussions held above, I am of the view that, the evidence of the PW1 and the documentary evidence placed by the petitioner substantiate the case of the petitioner.

Hence, I am of the opinion that, petitioner has proved its case that, the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle Tata ACE vehicle bearing registration No.KA 04AA 4212.
In the said accident, the defending vehicle BMTC bus, bearing registration No.KA 57F1835, belonged to the petitioner was damaged.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO. 2:
20.

The petitioner being the owner of the defending vehicle bearing registration No.KA57F 1835,
asserting herein that, after the accident, vehicle in question belonged to the petitioner was fully damaged.
And in toto, the petitioner had suffered a loss of Rs.1,50,000/ .

In the evidence of PW1,
clearly stated that, due to the accident, following damages were caused to the BMTC bearing registration No.KA57F1835 noted as follows.:
" front windshield glass was completely broken. And left side bumper and body shape were damaged. "
21.On the other hand

, on going through the report of the motor vehicle inspector marked at Ex.P.9,
with respect to the damages of BMTC volvo bus bearing registration NO.KA57F1835 is concerned, noted in the said document as follows:
Front side wind screen glass broken. Front left side shape damaged.
22.
Apart form this, petitioner has produced trip sheets as per Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.3, job card as per Ex.P.8 and Ex.P.10 with respect to the income and loss pertaining to the vehicle in question.

Apart from this, placed the evidence of PW2, by name Wilson Lobo, who being the Depot Manager of the Bangalore Metropolitan vs ) Shri Pradeep.V on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61948013/
5 BMTC Depot No.25, in his evidence deposed with respect to the accident and damage caused to the bus in question.

Depot Manager of the Bangalore Metropolitan vs ) Shri Pradeep.V on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61948013/
5
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In para No.3 of his examination in chief evidence and in para No.4, he deposed that, as the result of the accident, bus was badly damaged, consequently bus was unable to complete the trip.
In this regard, the petitioner corporation had undergone repair charges of Rs.11,576/ and cancellation of trip on 8.5.2018, total loss of Rs.9,512/ was caused.
Further deposed that, due to accident, bus was unable to give service for six days causing loss of Rs.14,000/ per day and Rs.84,000/ for six days.
Apart from this, suffered loss of Rs.45,000/ towards damages, in toto Rs.1,50,000/ total loss suffered by the petitioner corporation.
In support of the evidence of this witness, produced Ex.P.13 to Ex.P.21 for consideration.

23. Along with the evidence of PW1 and PW2, on going through the material documents, reveal that, in the trip sheets Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.3 there is a clear mention about plying of the defending vehicle in question, as on the date of the accident.
And in the Ex.P.10, in column No.3 total loss noted as Rs.9,512/ and in column No.6, loss was mentioned as Rs.93,512/.
But, the said amount was written in the hand writing, in the typed copy.
No supportive documentary evidence is available on record, in proof of the said writing.
In the Ex.P.14, there is a mention about the purchase of spare parts, but no receipts on record to show, what amount has been paid towards the purchase of the said spare parts.

In the Ex.P.15, the damages of the vehicle in question were noted as follows:
"-57-F-1835     ,   
.      
 .     .   
    .  1  . 
    ."
24.
On the other hand, Ex.P.16 to Ex.P.21, disclose about in and out registers, work charts and daily income and expenditure registers.

These documents will not support the stand of the PW1 and PW2 to the effect that, due to the damages of the bus the petitioner corporation incurred a loss of Rs.1,50,000/.
25.

At the time of crossexamination of PW1, answers given by the PW1 reveals that, on the same date of sending the vehicle for repair, the bus in question was out from the workshop and denied the suggestion that, Ex.P.10 is the created document.
And admitted that, the corporation has not placed bills for having paid the expenses of the purchasing of spare parts of the bus and also not produced trip cancelled document.

Further, some of the answers given by the PW1 discloses that, in connection with loss of Rs.14,000 per day and damages of Rs.45,000/ no iota of documents were placed on record, in proof of the said assertion.
At the time of crossexamination of PW2, stated that, on 13 th the vehicle was returned after its repair.
And admitted that, no receipt placed for having purchased spare parts, since the said parts are available in the workshop itself belonged to their corporation.
And denied the suggestion that, the recitals of Ex.P.8, and the amount mentioned in the said document is approximate expenses incurred towards repair of the bus in question.

26. Over all appreciation of the documents and the evidence given by the PW1 and PW2, I am of the view that, the petitioner corporation has not placed satisfactory and convincing documents to show Bangalore Metropolitan vs ) Shri Pradeep.V on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61948013/
6
that, a sum of Rs.1,50,000/ loss of was caused to the corporation.

Hence, by considering the Ex.P.8, Ex.P.10 and Ex.P.14 to Ex.P.21 documents, placed by the petitioner corporation, along with the damages noted in the report of the motor vehicle inspector marked at Ex.P.9, I am of the view that, it is apt to award compensation of Rs.50,000/ towards damages of the vehicle.
The same will meet the ends of justice.

27. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, keeping in mind about the damages mentioned in the recitals of the IMV report, and also inconvenience caused to the petitioner, due to the said damage, I am of the view that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/
(Rupees Fifty Thousand only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.

LIABILITY:
28.

In so far as, liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner corporation that, due to the accident, caused by the driver of the offending vehicle the vehicle belong to the petitioner was damaged.
As such, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

29. On the other hand, the respondent No.2, through the evidence of RW1 strongly contended that,
at the time of accident, the driver of the offending vehicle TATA ACE bearing registration No.KA 04AA4212 was not holding valid driving licence to drive the vehicle at the time of accident.
The said allegation remained unquestioned by the owner or driver of the offending vehicle.
As per the contention of the company, the insured has violated the terms and conditions of the policy, though it was valid as on the date of the accident as per Ex.R.1.

No doubt, the prosecution papers especially charge sheet submitted by the investigation officer clearly evident that, at the time of accident,
driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence.

In such a situation the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle cannot escape from liability to pay compensation to the petitioner corporation towards the damages caused to their vehicle.

30. In view of propositions laid down in several cases by the Hon'ble Apex Court and also by out own Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, since the petition has been filed under beneficial legislation the principle of pay and recover has to be followed as discussed in detail in Swaran Singh's case and other relevant subsequent cases.
In the light of my due discussions held above, it is relevant to note that, the doctrine of pay and recover has been considered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Swaran Singh's Case and in Pappu's case.

And the said judgments of the Honourable Apex Court were not over ruled till today, and the propositions laid down in the said judgments, remained intact and the said judgments till today are in force.
Hence, to protect the interest of third party, it is apt in the case on hand, to follow the doctrine of pay and recover.
Since as per Article 12 of the Constitution of India, company also comes under the concept of State.
As such, it is the duty of the State to protect the interest of the third party.

31. In the light of my detailed discussion held above, I am of the view that, though the respondent No.1, being the owner of the offending vehicle cannot escape from his liability to pay compensation Bangalore Metropolitan vs ) Shri Pradeep.

V on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61948013/
7 to the petitioner, in view of violation of terms and conditions of the policy, and to protect the interest of the third party, it is necessary to direct the insurance company to pay compensation to the petitioner and thereafter to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle, through due process of law.

32 As such, the respondent No.2, being the insurance company has to satisfy the award and recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle who is the respondent No.1 in the case on hand, in view of the valid insurance policy.
As such, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Thereafter, recover the same from the owner through due process of law.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
33.

In view of due discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
*O R D E R*
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act, is hereby partly allowed with cost.

Consequently, the petitioner is entitle for damages of Rs.50,000/ (Rupees Fifty Thousand only)
along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.

The respondent No.2 being the insurance company, is liable to pay the compensation determined by this court, with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order, at the first instance, thereafter, recover the same, from the respondent No.1, who is the owner of the offending vehicle, in accordance with law.
After deposit of the award amount with interest, since the compensation amount is meager, the entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.500/.
Draw award accordingly.
(*Dictated to the stenographer through online, corrected by me and then pronounced in open court on this the 20th day of January 2023*).
